turn_text: Last week our guest on this program was Senator Tester from Montana. You've talked about the price discovery for cattle for some time. Where is this now and why do you feel like your legislation is the right way to go?

The reason my legislation is the right way to go is because first of all I had 150 farmers in Jones County, Iowa say that it was the right direction to go even though I had to introduce the bill without talking to them but it's pretty simple. You have four big packers controlling eighty percent of the slaughter of that eighty of that hundred percent of that slaughter less than twenty percent of it is available for the spot market about sixty percent of the cattle in Iowa marketed on a spot market basis so you're a farmer you call up you're finding out that they can't take your cattle for a month if you get a price is probably a lot less than other people are getting that same day You don't really know whether you're getting a fair price because there's not enough spot market sales to know exactly what a fair price is. And so my bill would be pretty simple. It would open up instead of less than 20% of the market being available for the negotiated price of a day. It would be 50%. Now, maybe 50% is too high. And we had a hearing on this before the Senate Agriculture Committee. I think it backed up the need for our legislation before the end of July. We're going to have a hearing before the Judiciary Committee. on antitrust aspects of it, and I hope the House Agriculture Committee. I went to the House Representatives Office of the Chairman of that committee, talked to him a couple months ago about looking into this issue, and I thought he was open to doing that. So I hope we can pass some legislation that will get a fair price for spot market farmers and be able to deliver your cattle a lot sooner than three or four weeks out.
